title: Minimal attack surface — only 3 TCP ports open
description: Full TCP scan (all 65535 ports) shows only 22/SSH, 80/HTTP, 443/HTTPS open. All others closed.
risks: Low attack surface reduces exposure but focus exploitation on these 3 services.
attack_vectors: Target SSH brute-force, web app vulns on 80/443, SSL/TLS weaknesses.
proof_of_existence: PORT STATE SERVICE VERSION 22/tcp open ssh OpenSSH 9.6p1 Ubuntu 80/tcp open http nginx 1.24.0 443/tcp open ssl/http nginx 1.24.0. Not shown: 65532 closed tcp ports (reset)
remediation: Maintain minimal port exposure; ensure all 3 services are hardened.

title: OpenSSH 9.6p1 exposed on port 22
description: OpenSSH 9.6p1 Ubuntu 3ubuntu13.18 running with ECDSA and ED25519 host keys.
risks: SSH exposed to internet; potential brute-force or credential stuffing attacks.
attack_vectors: SSH brute-force, credential stuffing, exploit any OpenSSH vulnerabilities.
proof_of_existence: 22/tcp open ssh OpenSSH 9.6p1 Ubuntu 3ubuntu13.18 (Ubuntu Linux; protocol 2.0) ssh-hostkey: 256 df:f6:b1 (ECDSA) 256 fb:00:5b (ED25519)
remediation: Disable password auth, use key-only, restrict by IP, change default port.

title: Nginx 1.24.0 version disclosed on HTTP and HTTPS
description: Server header reveals nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu) on both port 80 and 443.
risks: Version disclosure enables targeted exploit selection against known nginx CVEs.
attack_vectors: Search for nginx 1.24.0 specific CVEs; attempt config disclosure or path traversal.
proof_of_existence: http-server-header: nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu) on both port 80 and 443
remediation: Set server_tokens off in nginx config to hide version info.

title: HTTP port 80 missing X-Frame-Options header
description: Nikto reports X-Frame-Options not present on port 80 (HTTP). HTTPS port 443 has it.
risks: Clickjacking possible on HTTP responses before redirect to HTTPS.
attack_vectors: Embed HTTP response in iframe before 301 redirect for clickjacking attack.
proof_of_existence: Nikto: The anti-clickjacking X-Frame-Options header is not present. (port 80)
remediation: Add X-Frame-Options header to HTTP server block on port 80.

title: CSP allows unsafe-inline for scripts and styles
description: Content-Security-Policy includes 'unsafe-inline' for both script-src and style-src directives.
risks: XSS attacks can execute inline scripts bypassing CSP; increases XSS impact.
attack_vectors: Inject inline JavaScript via any input vector; CSP won't block execution.
remediation: Remove 'unsafe-inline'; use nonces or hashes for inline scripts/styles.

title: Developer email and author metadata exposed
description: Page source contains meta author 'Ahmed Chiboub' and email ahmed.chiboub@cyberian-defenses.com.
risks: Email can be used for phishing, OSINT, credential stuffing, and social engineering.
attack_vectors: Use email for targeted phishing, password spray, or social engineering.
remediation: Remove personal email from page source; use generic contact form.

title: Hidden /blog/ directory and /robots.txt discovered
description: Nmap http-enum found /blog/ (Blog) and /robots.txt accessible on the web server.
risks: Blog may contain additional endpoints, sensitive info, or outdated plugins.
attack_vectors: Enumerate /blog/ for content management system, plugins, user enumeration.
remediation: Review /robots.txt for sensitive path disclosures; secure /blog/.

title: All UDP ports scanned are closed
risks: No UDP services exposed; reduces amplification attack surface.
proof_of_existence: All 11 UDP ports show STATE: closed (domain, tftp, ntp, netbios, snmp, etc.)
remediation: No action needed; maintain closed UDP posture.

title: rDNS reveals Hostinger cloud hosting
description: Reverse DNS shows 76.13.46.223 resolves to srv1479954.hstgr.cloud (Hostinger cloud).
risks: Shared hosting environment may have co-tenant risks; cloud provider targeting.
attack_vectors: Check for Hostinger-specific vulnerabilities or shared infrastructure issues.
remediation: Ensure cloud instance isolation; review Hostinger security settings.

title: SSL certificate nearing expiration (Oct 2026)
description: Let's Encrypt cert valid 2026-07-25 to 2026-10-23. EC key 256-bit, ECDSA-SHA384.
risks: Cert expires in ~2 months; if not auto-renewed, HTTPS will fail.
attack_vectors: If cert expires and isn't renewed, users face cert warnings enabling MITM.
proof_of_existence: Not valid before: 2026-07-25 Not valid after: 2026-10-23 Issuer: Let's Encrypt EC 256-bit
remediation: Ensure Let's Encrypt auto-renewal is configured and monitored.
